agent.name: Flag
agent.strategy: Bull flag: pole, quiet drift, breakout
agent.description: Well-formed bull flags across the universe: forming flags with their trigger and stop, and breakouts on volume with the trade attached.

context.label: Well-formed
context.value: flag vol <= 70% of pole, pullback <= 40%, 5-8 sessions

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 30% pole · 5-session flag · 25% pullback on 69% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This is a textbook-clean flag structurally—tight consolidation, volume decay, shallow retracement—but the 11% gap up *into* the breakout is a red flag: it suggests conviction already priced in, leaving little fresh fuel. Confirmation would require a close above $61.92 on volume exceeding the pole; breakdown would confirm if it closes below $58.28 on any volume spike, especially if it revisits the flag low. Without a fresh catalyst post-gap, this has the setup of a flag that's already been half-traded by momentum players.

The breakout would need a decisive close above $77.96 on volume matching or exceeding the pole's average to have any edge; a drop below $76.51 on volume would likely cascade lower, given that most half-formed flags fail.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 19% pole · 5-session flag · 36% pullback on 63% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag is **messy, not clean**: the 36% retracement is shallow (flags typically hold 33-50%, so marginal), and critically, the consolidation occurred on only 63% of pole volume—weak absorption that suggests buyers aren't confident enough to defend support. The breakout trigger at $28.82 needs to close above it on expanding volume (ideally 100%+ of pole) to show conviction; if it stalls there or closes below $28.50, the flag likely dissolves into a failed breakout pattern with $27.58 as the next test.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 20% pole · 5-session flag · 30% pullback on 43% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning: This flag setup lacks conviction: the pullback consumed 70% of the pole's gains (not the typical 25-50%), and lighter volume during consolidation often signals weak accumulation rather than coiled strength. Confirmation would require a decisive break above $84.56 on volume expansion matching or exceeding the pole's average; breakdown below $80.27 would confirm the flag failed and suggest the initial move was a false breakout. The forming stage is the weakest link in flag performance—statistically, waiting for either clean confirmation or invalidation is prudent before committing capital.

setup.title: Flag
setup.label: 16% pole · 5-session flag · 32% pullback on 64% of pole volume

opportunities.reasoning:
# DCOM Bull Flag Assessment

This is a **marginally clean flag setup undermined by weak conviction**: the 5-session consolidation is tight and well-proportioned, but the pole itself is thin (16% move) and the flag's volume compression to 64% of pole volume suggests sellers aren't capitulating. 

**Confirmation would require** a decisive close above $42.41 on expanding volume (ideally matching or exceeding pole volume) with momentum follow-through; **killshot is** a retest and break below $41.44 on volume, which would suggest the flag was merely a failed breakdown attempt rather than a coiling spring. Given that forming flags historically break down more often than up, waiting for both price and volume confirmation at trigger is critical.
